title: The Stone Memory Where Compression Becomes Story

features.name: folded stone face
features.desc-on-touch: You place your hand on rock that remembers being folded, layer on layer. Pressure wrote its history here. The archive reads: this is what being kept looks like.

features.name: compressed evidence
features.desc-on-touch: Fossils pressed into the stone: shells, ferns, creatures whose names are older than naming. The archive holds them. Weight made them permanent.

features.name: deep measurement
features.desc-on-touch: A survey mark, hammered in before half the trees that grow here were born. The stone remembers what the surveyor was measuring for. It still waits for the answer.

features.name: water-carved channel
features.desc-on-touch: A groove worn by decades of water finding the same path down the stone. You trace it: this is how a rock learns it has a story written on it by what passes through.

features.name: casing echo
features.desc-on-touch: Here, another archive left its mark—a solar casing bolted to the stone years ago, then removed. The bolt-holes remain. History is a negative space.

features.name: reading point
features.desc-on-touch: Lichen blooms here in patterns that the archive's own render mimics. You wonder: is the stone reading the lichen, or is the lichen reading the stone?

inscription: here the earth holds what time has pressed into stillness

reverie.title: REVERIE — stone holding deep time
narr: You both kneel at the erosion gully, Katita sketching
the folded strata while Leif photographs. She says: what
if the archive itself is just a small copying of what
the earth has been doing for millions of years. He nods,
focuses. The stone around you is patient. Its memory
is older than words, and you are learning its language.

exits.label: back down into the bedrock heartbeat
deeper into the roots that remember being folded
across to the limestone caverns where water wrote differently
